\n\n

గణన:

\n\n

అమ్మకపు ధర = కిలోకు ₹75

\n\n

లాభం = 20%

\n\n

⇒ మిశ్రమం కొన్న ధర = అమ్మకపు ధర / (1 + లాభం%)

\n\n

⇒ మిశ్రమం కొన్న ధర = ₹75 / (1 + 0.20)

\n\n

⇒ మిశ్రమం కొన్న ధర = ₹75 / 1.20

\n\n

⇒ మిశ్రమం కొన్న ధర = కిలోకు ₹62.50

\n\n

ఆరోపణ పద్ధతిని ఉపయోగించి:

\n\n

⇒ \\(\\frac{\\text{చక్కెర 1 పరిమాణం}}{\\text{చక్కెర 2 పరిమాణం}} = \\frac{46 - 62.50}{62.50 - 78} \\)

\n\n

⇒ \\(\\frac{\\text{చక్కెర 1 పరిమాణం}}{\\text{చక్కెర 2 పరిమాణం}} = \\frac{-16.50}{-15.50} \\)

\n\n

⇒ \\(\\frac{\\text{చక్కెర 1 పరిమాణం}}{\\text{చక్కెర 2 పరిమాణం}} = \\frac{16.50}{15.50} \\)

\n\n

⇒ \\(\\frac{\\text{చక్కెర 1 పరిమాణం}}{\\text{చక్కెర 2 పరిమాణం}} = \\frac{33}{31} \\)

\n\n

సరైన సమాధానం ఆప్షన్ 4: 33 : 31.

\n\n

ব্যবহৃত সূত্র:

\n\n

বিক্রয় মূল্য = ক্রয় মূল্য + লাভ

\n\n

লাভ = (বিক্রয় মূল্য - ক্রয় মূল্য)/(ক্রয় মূল্য) × 100

\n\n

\\(\\frac{\\text{Quantity of sugar 1}}{\\text{Quantity of sugar 2}} = \\frac{C_2 - C}{C - C_1} \\)

\n\n

অ্যালিগেশন পদ্ধতি ব্যবহার করে:

ಇಲ್ಲಿ C1\" id=\"MathJax-Element-1-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">C1C1\" id=\"MathJax-Element-445-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">C1C1\" id=\"MathJax-Element-1117-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">C1C1\" id=\"MathJax-Element-13-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">C1C1\n\n ಸಕ್ಕರೆ 1 ರ ಖರೀದಿ ಬೆಲೆ, C2\" id=\"MathJax-Element-2-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">C2C2\" id=\"MathJax-Element-446-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">C2C2\" id=\"MathJax-Element-1118-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">C2C2\" id=\"MathJax-Element-14-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">C2C2\n\n ಸಕ್ಕರೆ 2 ರ ಖರೀದಿ ಬೆಲೆ, ಮತ್ತು C\" id=\"MathJax-Element-3-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">CC\" id=\"MathJax-Element-447-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">CC\" id=\"MathJax-Element-1119-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">CC\" id=\"MathJax-Element-15-Frame\" role=\"presentation\" style=\"position: relative;\" tabindex=\"0\">CC\n\n ಮಿಶ್ರಣದ ಖರೀದಿ ಬೆಲೆ.

\n\n

ಮಾರಾಟ ಬೆಲೆ = ₹75 ಪ್ರತಿ ಕೆ.ಜಿ.

ಲಾಭ = 20%

⇒ ಮಿಶ್ರಣದ ಖರೀದಿ ಬೆಲೆ = ಮಾರಾಟ ಬೆಲೆ / (1 + ಲಾಭ%)

\n\n

\n\n

\n\n

⇒ ಮಿಶ್ರಣದ ಖರೀದಿ ಬೆಲೆ = ₹62.50 ಪ್ರತಿ ಕೆ.ಜಿ.

\n\n

Shortcut Trick\n

Since the time of running is constant for both, the ratio of distances covered is equal to the ratio of their speeds.

\n

Ratio of speeds (Police : Thief) = 23 : 21

\n

Difference in distance ratio = 23 − 21 = 2 units, which is equal to the initial gap of 100 m.

\n

⇒ 1 unit = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 m

\n

⇒ Distance run by the thief = 21 units = 21 × 50 = 1050 m

\n

∴ The correct answer is 1050 m.

\n\n

Alternate Method

\n\n

Given:

\n

Distance between policeman and thief = 100 m

\n

Speed of thief = 21 km/h

\n

Speed of policeman = 23 km/h

\n

Formula Used:

\n

Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed1 − Speed2

\n

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

\n

Distance = Speed × Time

\n

Calculations:

\n

⇒ Relative speed = 23 − 21 = 2 km/h

\n

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 2 × (5 ÷ 18) = 5/9 m/s

\n

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 100 ÷ (5/9) = 180 seconds

\n

⇒ Distance covered by the thief = Speed of thief × Time taken

\n

⇒ Distance covered = [21 × (5 ÷ 18)] × 180

\n

⇒ Distance covered = 21 × 50 = 1050 m

\n

∴ The correct answer is 1050 m.

\n\n

Additional Information

\n

Relative Speed in Same Direction

\n

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Srelative = |S1 − S2|.

\n

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

\n

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Srelative = S1 + S2.

\n

Proportionality of Distance and Speed

\n

When the time traveled is constant, the distance covered is directly proportional to the speed: D1/D2 = S1/S2.

दिया गया है:

\n\n

चोर और पुलिसकर्मी के बीच की दूरी = 100 मीटर

\n\n

चोर की गति = 21 किमी/घंटा

\n\n

पुलिसकर्मी की गति = 23 किमी/घंटा

\n\n

प्रयुक्त सूत्र:

\n\n

सापेक्ष गति = पुलिसकर्मी की गति - चोर की गति

\n\n

समय = दूरी / सापेक्ष गति

\n\n

चोर द्वारा तय की गई दूरी = चोर की गति x समय

\n\n

गणना:

\n\n

सापेक्ष गति = 23 किमी/घंटा - 21 किमी/घंटा

\n\n

सापेक्ष गति = 2 किमी/घंटा

\n\n

2 किमी/घंटा को मीटर/सेकेंड में बदलिए:

\n\n

1 किमी/घंटा = 5/18 मीटर/सेकेंड

\n\n

2 किमी/घंटा = 2 x (5/18) मीटर/सेकेंड

\n\n

2 किमी/घंटा = 10/18 मीटर/सेकेंड

\n\n

2 किमी/घंटा = 5/9 मीटर/सेकेंड

\n\n

100 मीटर की दूरी तय करने में लगा समय:

\n\n

समय = 100 मीटर / (5/9 मीटर/सेकेंड)

\n\n

⇒ समय = 100 x (9/5) सेकंड

\n\n

⇒ समय = 180 सेकंड

\n\n

चोर द्वारा तय की गई दूरी:

\n\n

चोर की गति मीटर/सेकेंड में = 21 x (5/18) मीटर/सेकेंड

\n\n

चोर की गति = 105/18 मीटर/सेकेंड

\n\n

चोर की गति = 35/6 मीटर/सेकेंड

\n\n

दूरी = गति x समय

\n\n

⇒ दूरी = (35/6) मीटर/सेकंड x 180 सेकंड

\n\n

⇒ दूरी = 35 x 30 मीटर

\n\n

⇒ दूरी = 1050 मीटर

\n\n

चोर को पकड़े जाने से पहले उसे 1050 मीटर भागना पड़ेगा।

ਚੋਰ ਦੀ ਗਤੀ = 21 ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ/ਘੰਟਾ

\n\n

ਪੁਲਿਸ ਕਰਮੀ ਦੀ ਗਤੀ = 23 ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ/ਘੰਟਾ

\n\n

ਵਰਤਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਸੂਤਰ :

\n\n

ਸਾਪੇਖਿਕ ਗਤੀ = ਪੁਲਿਸ ਕਰਮੀ ਦੀ ਗਤੀ - ਚੋਰ ਦੀ ਗਤੀ

\n\n

ਸਮਾਂ = ਦੂਰੀ / ਸਾਪੇਖਿਕ ਗਤੀ

\n\n

ਚੋਰ ਦੁਆਰਾ ਤੈਅ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਦੂਰੀ = ਚੋਰ ਦੀ ਗਤੀ x ਸਮਾਂ

\n\n

ਗਣਨਾ:

\n\n

ਸਾਪੇਖਿਕ ਗਤੀ = 23 ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ/ਘੰਟਾ - 21 ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ/ਘੰਟਾ

\n\n

ਸਾਪੇਖਿਕ ਗਤੀ = 2 ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ/ਘੰਟਾ

\n\n

2 ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ/ਘੰਟਾ ਨੂੰ ਮੀਟਰ/ਸਕਿੰਟ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਦਲੋ:

\n\n

1 ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ/ਘੰਟਾ = 5/18 ਮੀਟਰ/ਸਕਿੰਟ

\n\n

2 ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ/ਘੰਟਾ = 2 x (5/18) ਮੀਟਰ/ਸਕਿੰਟ

\n\n

2 ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ/ਘੰਟਾ = 10/18 ਮੀਟਰ/ਸਕਿੰਟ

\n\n

2 ਕਿਲੋਮੀਟਰ/ਘੰਟਾ = 5/9 ਮੀਟਰ/ਸਕਿੰਟ

\n\n

100 ਮੀਟਰ ਦੀ ਦੂਰੀ ਤੈਅ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਲੱਗਿਆ ਸਮਾਂ:

\n\n

ਸਮਾਂ = 100 ਮੀਟਰ / (5/9 ਮੀਟਰ/ਸਕਿੰਟ)

\n\n

⇒ ਸਮਾਂ = 100 x (9/5) ਸਕਿੰਟ

\n\n

⇒ ਸਮਾਂ = 180 ਸਕਿੰਟ

\n\n

ਚੋਰ ਦੁਆਰਾ ਤੈਅ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਦੂਰੀ:

\n\n

ਚੋਰ ਦੀ ਗਤੀ ਮੀਟਰ/ਸਕਿੰਟ ਵਿੱਚ = 21 x (5/18) ਮੀਟਰ/ਸਕਿੰਟ

\n\n

Shortcut Trick\n

Rearrange the given expression to group similar terms together:

\n

⇒ [(3x − 2y) + 17] × [(3x − 2y) − 17]

\n

Apply the difference of squares formula (a + b)(a − b) = a2 − b2:

\n

⇒ (3x − 2y)2 − 172

\n

⇒ 9x2 − 12xy + 4y2 − 289

\n

∴ The correct answer is 9x2 − 12xy + 4y2 − 289.

\n\n

Alternate Method

\n

Given:

\n

Expression: (3x + 17 − 2y)(3x − 17 − 2y)

\n

Formula Used:

\n

Distributive property: (a + b + c)(d + e + f) = ad + ae + af + bd + be + bf + cd + ce + cf

\n

Calculations:

\n

Multiply each term of the first polynomial by each term of the second polynomial:

\n

⇒ 3x(3x − 17 − 2y) + 17(3x − 17 − 2y) − 2y(3x − 17 − 2y)

\n

⇒ (9x2 − 51x − 6xy) + (51x − 289 − 34y) + (−6xy + 34y + 4y2)

\n

Combine the like terms:

\n

⇒ 9x2 + (−51x + 51x) + (−6xy − 6xy) + (−34y + 34y) + 4y2 − 289

\n

⇒ 9x2 + 0 − 12xy + 0 + 4y2 − 289

\n

⇒ 9x2 − 12xy + 4y2 − 289

\n

∴ The correct answer is 9x2 − 12xy + 4y2 − 289.

\n\n

Additional Information

\n

Standard Algebraic Identities

\n

Some common and useful algebraic identities include (a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2, (a − b)2 = a2 − 2ab + b2, and a2 − b2 = (a + b)(a − b).

\n

Distributive Property in Polynomials

\n

When multiplying two polynomials, you must multiply each term in the first polynomial by every term in the second polynomial. Grouping and combining like terms simplifies the final expression efficiently.

Percentage Increase = [(New Value - Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100

\n\n

⇒ Percentage Increase = 15%

\n\n

∴ The percentage increase in students passing out in 2022 compared to 2021 is 15%.

\n\n

∴ 2021 की तुलना में 2022 में उत्तीर्ण विद्यार्थियों में प्रतिशत वृद्धि 15% है।

\n", "te": "", "mr": "", "bn": "", "ml": "", "gu": "", "kn": "", "ta": "", "or": "", "as": "", "ks": "", "kok": "", "mni": "", "ne": "", "pa": "", "sd": "", "ur": "", "sat": "", "mai": "", "brx": "", "doi": "", "sa": "", "grt": "", "kha": "", "lus": "", "bo": "", "trp": ""}, "tags": ["Tabulation"], "concept": "Data Interpretation", "confidence": "high"}, {"qid": "671604913e74343140712fab", "qs_no": 18, "pos_marks": 2.0, "neg_marks": 0.5, "type": "mcq", "langs": {"en": {"value": "A, B and C invested money in a business such that 2 times A's share, 4 times B's share and 6 times C's share are all equal. If they earned ₹44,000, find the share of A.", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "₹22,000"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "₹12,000"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "₹24,000"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "₹20,000"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}, "hn": {"value": "A, B और C एक व्यापार में धन निवेश करते हैं जिससे A के हिस्से का 2 गुना, B के हिस्से का 4 गुना और C के हिस्से का 6 गुना सभी बराबर हैं। यदि वे ₹44,000 अर्जित करते हैं, तो A का हिस्सा ज्ञात कीजिए।", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "₹22,000"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "₹12,000"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "₹24,000"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "₹20,000"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "3", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

Shortcut Trick\n

Inverse ratio of 2A = 4B = 6C gives A : B : C = (1/2) : (1/4) : (1/6) = 6 : 3 : 2.

\n

Total share parts = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 parts.

\n

11 parts → ₹44,000

\n

1 part → ₹4,000

\n

A's share = 6 parts × 4,000 = ₹24,000.

\n

∴ The correct answer is ₹24,000.

\n

Alternate Method

\n

Given:

\n

2 × A's share = 4 × B's share = 6 × C's share

\n

Total profit earned = ₹44,000

\n\n

Calculations:

\n

⇒ Let 2A = 4B = 6C = LCM(2, 4, 6)

\n

⇒ LCM of 2, 4, and 6 = 12

\n

⇒ 2A = 12 → A = 6

\n

⇒ 4B = 12 → B = 3

\n

⇒ 6C = 12 → C = 2

\n

⇒ The ratio of their investments A : B : C = 6 : 3 : 2

\n

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 parts

\n

⇒ 11 parts = ₹44,000

\n

⇒ 1 part = 44,000 ÷ 11 = ₹4,000

\n

⇒ Share of A = 6 parts = 6 × 4,000 = ₹24,000

\n

∴ The correct answer is ₹24,000.

\n

Additional Information

\n

Compound Partnership

\n

When investments are made for different time periods, the profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of capital and time. Profit Ratio = (C1 × T1) : (C2 × T2).

\n

Active vs Sleeping Partner

\n

An active partner manages the business and typically receives a salary or commission before the remaining profit is divided. A sleeping partner only invests capital without managing the affairs.

\n

Equality of Multiples Trick

\n

If given aA = bB = cC, the quickest way to find the ratio A : B : C is by taking the LCM of a, b, and c and dividing the LCM by each corresponding coefficient.

A के हिस्से का 2 गुना = B के हिस्से का 4 गुना = C के हिस्से का 6 गुना

\n\n

कुल आय = ₹44,000

\n\n

प्रयुक्त सूत्र:

\n\n

A का हिस्सा + B का हिस्सा + C का हिस्सा = कुल आय

\n\n

गणना:

\n\n

मान लीजिए A का हिस्सा a, B का हिस्सा b और C का हिस्सा c है।

\n\n

दिया गया है: 2a = 4b = 6c

\n\n

⇒ a = 2b

\n\n

⇒ a = 3c

\n\n

हम b और c को a के पदों में व्यक्त कर सकते हैं:

\n\n

b = a/2

\n\n

c = a/3

\n\n

इसलिए, A का हिस्सा + B का हिस्सा + C का हिस्सा = कुल आय

\n\n

a + a/2 + a/3 = 44000

\n\n

समीकरण को हल करने के लिए, एक समान हर ज्ञात कीजिए:

\n\n

\\(a + \\frac{a}{2} + \\frac{a}{3} = 44000\\)

\n\n

⇒ \\(\\frac{6a + 3a + 2a}{6} = 44000\\)

\n\n

⇒ \\(\\frac{11a}{6} = 44000\\)

\n\n

⇒ 11a = 44000 × 6

\n\n

⇒ 11a = 264000

\n\n

⇒ a = 264000 / 11

\n\n

⇒ a = 24000

\n\n

A का हिस्सा ₹24,000 है।

Shortcut Trick\n

Total SP = ₹1260 + ₹1440 = ₹2700

\n

Total CP = 1260 × (100 ÷ 125) + 1440 × (100 ÷ 90) = ₹1008 + ₹1600 = ₹2608

\n

Overall Gain = Total SP − Total CP = 2700 − 2608 = ₹92

\n

Gain % = (92 ÷ 2608) × 100 = 575 ÷ 163 = 3 86/163%

\n

∴ The correct answer is 3 86/163% Gain.

\n\n

Alternate Method

\n\n

Given:

\n

Selling Price (SP) of first keyboard = ₹1260, Profit = 25%

\n

Selling Price (SP) of second keyboard = ₹1440, Loss = 10%

\n\n

Formula Used:

\n

Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)] × SP

\n

Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)] × SP

\n

Gain % = (Gain ÷ Total CP) × 100

\n\n\n\n

Calculations:

\n

⇒ CP of first keyboard = (100 ÷ 125) × 1260 = (4 ÷ 5) × 1260 = ₹1008

\n

⇒ CP of second keyboard = (100 ÷ 90) × 1440 = (10 ÷ 9) × 1440 = ₹1600

\n

⇒ Total CP = 1008 + 1600 = ₹2608

\n

⇒ Total SP = 1260 + 1440 = ₹2700

\n

⇒ Total Gain = Total SP − Total CP = 2700 − 2608 = ₹92

\n

⇒ Gain Percentage = (92 ÷ 2608) × 100

\n

⇒ Gain Percentage = 9200 ÷ 2608 = 2300 ÷ 652

\n

⇒ Gain Percentage = 575 ÷ 163 = 3 86/163%

\n

∴ The correct answer is 3 86/163% Gain.

\n\n

Additional Information

\n\n

Overall Profit or Loss on Same Selling Price

\n

When two identical items are sold at the same selling price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always an overall loss given by Loss% = (x ÷ 10)2. In this problem, selling prices are different, so individual calculation was required.

\n\n

Marked Price and Discount

\n

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100. This relationship is useful when the items are sold after offering a flat discount on the catalog or marked price.

\n\n

Dishonest Dealer Concept

\n

When a dealer claims to sell items at his cost price but uses a false weight, his profit percent is evaluated as: Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

दिया गया है:

\n\n

पहले कीबोर्ड का विक्रय मूल्य = ₹1,260

\n\n

पहले कीबोर्ड पर लाभ = 25%

\n\n

दूसरे कीबोर्ड का विक्रय मूल्य = ₹1,440

\n\n

दूसरे कीबोर्ड पर हानि = 10%

\n\n

प्रयुक्त सूत्र:

\n\n

क्रय मूल्य (CP) = विक्रय मूल्य (SP) / (1 + लाभ%)

\n\n

क्रय मूल्य (CP) = विक्रय मूल्य (SP) / (1 - हानि%)

\n\n

कुल लाभ या हानि प्रतिशत = (कुल लाभ या हानि / कुल क्रय मूल्य) × 100%

\n\n

गणना:

\n\n

पहले कीबोर्ड के लिए:

\n\n

CP1 = 1260 / (1 + 0.25)

\n\n

⇒ CP1 = 1260 / 1.25

\n\n

⇒ CP1 = 1008

\n\n

दूसरे कीबोर्ड के लिए:

\n\n

CP2 = 1440 / (1 - 0.10)

\n\n

⇒ CP2 = 1440 / 0.90

\n\n

⇒ CP2 = 1600

\n\n

कुल CP = CP1 + CP2

\n\n

⇒ कुल CP = 1008 + 1600

\n\n

⇒ कुल CP = 2608

\n\n

कुल SP = 1260 + 1440

\n\n

⇒ कुल SP = 2700

\n\n

कुल लाभ = कुल SP - कुल CP

\n\n

⇒ कुल लाभ = 2700 - 2608

\n\n

⇒ कुल लाभ = 92

\n\n

कुल लाभ प्रतिशत = (कुल लाभ / कुल CP) × 100%

\n\n

⇒ कुल लाभ प्रतिशत = (92 / 2608) × 100%

\n\n

⇒ कुल लाभ प्रतिशत = 3 \\(\\frac{86}{163}\\) %

\n\n

कुल लाभ प्रतिशत 3 \\(\\frac{86}{163}\\) % है।

Shortcut Trick\n

In congruent triangles, corresponding parts are equal. Since ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR, we know that ∠A = ∠P.

\n

The sum of the internal angles in ΔABC is 180º, which gives us ∠A + ∠C = 180º − ∠B.

\n

Substitute ∠A with ∠P directly: ∠P + ∠C = 180º − 35º = 145º.

{"prompt": "2", "value": "10,560"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "9,230"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "10,230"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "2", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

Shortcut Trick\n

Selling Price can be calculated directly by applying successive discount percentage multipliers to the Marked Price.

\n

SP = MP × (100 − D1)% × (100 − D2)%

\n

SP = 15000 × 80% × 88%

\n

SP = 15000 × 0.80 × 0.88 = 12000 × 0.88 = 10560

\n

∴ The correct answer is ₹10,560.

\n

Alternate Method

\n

Given:

\n

Marked Price (MP) = ₹15,000

\n

First discount (D1) = 20%

\n

Second discount (D2) = 12%

\n

Formula Used:

\n

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D1)/100 × (100 − D2)/100

\n\n

Calculations:

\n

⇒ SP = 15000 × (100 − 20)/100 × (100 − 12)/100

\n

⇒ SP = 15000 × (80/100) × (88/100)

\n

⇒ SP = 15000 × 4/5 × 22/25

\n

⇒ SP = 15000 × 88/125

\n

⇒ SP = 120 × 88

\n

⇒ SP = 10560

\n

∴ The correct answer is ₹10,560.

\n

Additional Information

\n

Effective Successive Discount

\n

When two successive discounts of d1% and d2% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage can be calculated directly using the formula: [d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2)/100]%.

\n

Marked Price vs Selling Price

\n

A discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP) of an item. The price obtained after deducting the discount is the final Selling Price (SP). The fundamental formula connects them as SP = MP − Discount.

\n

Relation between CP and MP

\n

If a profit of P% is made by a shopkeeper even after allowing a discount of D%, then the direct ratio between the Cost Price (CP) and the Marked Price (MP) is given by CP/MP = (100 − D)/(100 + P).

Shortcut Trick\n

The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

\n

Half of the chord length = 11 ÷ 2 = 5.5 cm.

\n

Using Pythagoras theorem to find the distance (d) from the centre directly:

\n

d = √(12.52 − 5.52) = √[(12.5 + 5.5) × (12.5 − 5.5)]

\n

d = √(18 × 7) = √126 ≈ 11.22 cm

\n

∴ The correct answer is 11.2 cm.

\n\n

Alternate Method

\n

\n

Radius of the circle (OA) = 12.5 cm

\n

Length of the chord (AB) = 11 cm

\n

Formula Used:

\n

दिया गया है:

\n\n

वृत्त की त्रिज्या (r) = 12.5 सेमी

\n\n

जीवा की लंबाई (c) = 11 सेमी

\n\n

प्रयुक्त सूत्र:

\n\n

केंद्र से जीवा की दूरी (d) की गणना निम्न सूत्र का उपयोग करके की जाती है:

\n\n

\\(d = \\sqrt{r^2 - \\left(\\frac{c}{2}\\right)^2}\\)

\n\n

गणना:

\n\n

जीवा की आधी लंबाई = c / 2 = 11 / 2 = 5.5 सेमी

\n\n

अब, सूत्र का उपयोग करने पर:

\n\n

⇒ \\(d = \\sqrt{12.5^2 - 5.5^2}\\)

\n\n

⇒ \\(d = \\sqrt{156.25 - 30.25}\\)

\n\n

⇒ \\(d = \\sqrt{126}\\)

\n\n

⇒ d ≈ 11.2 सेमी

\n\n

केंद्र से जीवा की दूरी 11.2 सेमी है।

\n

h = 600 ÷ (3.14 × 302)

\n

h = 600 ÷ 2826

\n

h ≈ 0.21 cm

\n

∴ The correct answer is 0.21 cm.

\n\n

Alternate Method

\n

\n

\n

\n

\n

Volume of a right circular cylinder = π × r2 × h

\n\n\n\n

Calculations:

\n

⇒ 600 = 3.14 × (30)2 × h

\n

⇒ 600 = 3.14 × 900 × h

\n

⇒ 600 = 2826 × h

\n

\n

\n

\n\n

Additional Information

\n

Curved Surface Area of a Cylinder

\n

The curved surface area (CSA) of a right circular cylinder is given by 2 × π × r × h.

\n

Total Surface Area of a Cylinder

\n

The total surface area (TSA) includes the CSA and the area of the two circular bases, given by 2 × π × r × (r + h).

\n

Volume of a Cone

\n

A cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder has exactly one-third of the cylinder's volume, given by (1 ÷ 3) × π × r2 × h.

If AB = 8 = PQ, BC = 10 = QR and ∠B = 35º, then what is the value of ∠P + ∠C?", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "145&ordm;"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "130&ordm;"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "160&ordm;"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "120&ordm;"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}, "hn": {"value": "△ABC और △PQR सर्वांगसम हैं। यदि AB = 8 = PQ, BC = 10 = QR और ∠B = 35° है, तो ∠P + ∠C का मान कितना है?", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "145&deg;"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "130&deg;"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "160&deg;"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "120&deg;"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "1", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

Shortcut Trick\n

In congruent triangles, corresponding parts are equal. Since ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR, we know that ∠A = ∠P.

\n

The sum of the internal angles in ΔABC is 180º, which gives us ∠A + ∠C = 180º − ∠B.

\n

Substitute ∠A with ∠P directly: ∠P + ∠C = 180º − 35º = 145º.

\n

∴ The correct answer is 145º.

\n\n

Alternate Method

\n

Given:

\n

ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR

\n

AB = PQ = 8 units, BC = QR = 10 units

\n

∠B = 35º

\n

Concept Used:

\n

If two triangles are congruent, their corresponding parts are equal (CPCTC).

\n

The sum of angles in a triangle is exactly 180º.

\n\n\n\n

Calculations:

\n

⇒ Since ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR, the corresponding angles map to each other in exactly the same order.

\n

⇒ ∠A = ∠P, ∠B = ∠Q, and ∠C = ∠R

\n

⇒ In ΔABC, the sum of internal angles equals 180º.

\n

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º

\n

⇒ Substitute the given value of ∠B = 35º into the equation:

\n

⇒ ∠A + 35º + ∠C = 180º

\n

⇒ ∠A + ∠C = 180º − 35º

\n

⇒ ∠A + ∠C = 145º

\n

⇒ Since ∠A = ∠P, substitute ∠A with ∠P in the equation:

\n

⇒ ∠P + ∠C = 145º

\n

∴ The correct answer is 145º.

\n\n

Additional Information

\n

Congruent Triangles (CPCTC)

\n

When two triangles are congruent, all of their corresponding sides and angles are equal. This property is known as Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent (CPCTC).

\n

Angle Sum Property of a Triangle

\n

The sum of all three internal angles of any planar triangle is strictly equal to 180º. i.e., ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º.

\n

Conditions for Congruency

\n

Two triangles can be proven congruent using five standard criteria: SSS (Side-Side-Side), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle), AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), and RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side).

\n\n

\n\n

△ABC में:

\n\n

\n\n

\n\n

\n\n

⇒ a + c = 145°

\n\n

\n\n

∠P + ∠C = a + c

\n\n

ऊपर की गणना से:

\n\n

⇒ a + c = 145°

\n\n

∠P + ∠C = 145°

\n\n

∠P + ∠C का मान 145° है।

M is a point on the circumference of the circle. If m∠MAP = 110º, then find the value of m∠MQA.", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "55&ordm;"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "35&ordm;"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "65&ordm;"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "70&ordm;"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}, "hn": {"value": "एक वृत्त जिसका केंद्र A है, उसके व्यास PQ है। वृत्त की परिधि पर एक बिंदु M है। यदि m∠MAP = 110° है, तो m∠MQA का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "55&deg;"}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "35&deg;"}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "65&deg;"}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "70&deg;"}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "1", "solution_html": {"en": "\n

Shortcut Trick\n

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is exactly double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

\n

Here, arc PM subtends ∠MAP at the centre A and ∠MQP at point Q on the circumference.

\n

⇒ ∠MQP = ∠MAP ÷ 2

\n

⇒ ∠MQA = 110º ÷ 2 = 55º

\n

∴ The correct answer is 55º.

\n\n

Alternate Method

\n\n\n\n

Given:

\n

PQ is the diameter of the circle with centre A.

\n

m∠MAP = 110º

\n

Concept Used:

\n

Angles on a straight line add up to 180º.

\n

Angles opposite to equal sides in an isosceles triangle are equal.

\n

The sum of all internal angles in a triangle is exactly 180º.

\n

Calculations:

\n

Since PAQ is a straight line, ∠MAP and ∠MAQ form a linear pair.

\n

⇒ ∠MAQ = 180º − ∠MAP

\n

⇒ ∠MAQ = 180º − 110º = 70º

\n

In ΔMAQ, the sides AM and AQ are radii of the same circle.

\n

⇒ AM = AQ

\n

Since opposite angles of equal sides are equal in a triangle:

\n

⇒ ∠AMQ = ∠MQA

\n

The sum of all angles in ΔMAQ is 180º:

\n

⇒ ∠MAQ + ∠AMQ + ∠MQA = 180º

\n

⇒ 70º + 2 × ∠MQA = 180º

\n

⇒ 2 × ∠MQA = 110º

\n

⇒ ∠MQA = 55º

\n

∴ The correct answer is 55º.

\n\n

Additional Information

\n\n

Angle at the Centre Theorem

\n

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is exactly double the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

\n\n

Angle in a Semicircle

\n

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always a right angle (90º).

\n\n

Angles in the Same Segment

\n

Angles subtended by the same arc at any two points on the circumference in the same segment of the circle are always equal.

दिया गया है:

\n\n

PQ केंद्र A वाले वृत्त का व्यास है।

\n\n

वृत्त की परिधि पर एक बिंदु M है।

\n\n

m∠MAP = 110°

\n\n

प्रयुक्त सूत्र:

\n\n

वृत्त के व्यास द्वारा परिधि पर बना कोण 90° होता है।

\n\n

त्रिभुज के कोणों का योग = 180°

\n\n

गणना:

\n\n

\n\n

त्रिभुज MAP में:

\n\n

⇒ ∠MAP = 110°

\n\n

चूँकि PQ व्यास है:

\n\n

⇒ ∠MAP + ∠MAQ = 180°

\n\n

⇒ 110° + ∠MAQ = 180°

\n\n

⇒ ∠MAQ = 180° - 110°

\n\n

⇒ ∠MAQ = 70°

\n\n

हमें ∠MQA ज्ञात करना है:

\n\n

त्रिभुज MAQ में:

\n\n

AQ = AM = वृत्त की त्रिज्या। इसलिए त्रिभुज MAQ समद्विबाहु है।

\n\n

इसलिए, ∠MQA = ∠QMA = x°

\n\n

⇒ 70° + x° + x° = 180°

\n\n

⇒ 70° + 2x° = 180°

\n\n

⇒ 2x° = 180° - 70°

\n\n

⇒ x° = 110/2

\n\n

⇒ x° = 55°

\n\n

∠MQA का मान 55° है।

Key Points

\n\n
    \n\t

  • When converting to the passive voice, the tense remains the same:
    • \n\t
  • has written → has been written

So, the correct passive construction is: A best-selling novel has been written by him.

Additional Information

\nHe wrote an inspiring speech for the event.", "options": [{"prompt": "1", "value": "An inspiring speech was being written by him for the event."}, {"prompt": "2", "value": "An inspiring speech was written by him for the event."}, {"prompt": "3", "value": "An inspiring speech is written by him for the event."}, {"prompt": "4", "value": "An inspiring speech has been written by him for the event."}], "range": {"start": "", "end": ""}}}, "correct_option": "2", "solution_html": {"en": "\n
The correct answer is Option 2.
\n\n
 
\n\n
Key Points
\n\n
    \n
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
    • \n
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: \"He wrote an inspiring speech for the event.\"
    • \n
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object \"an inspiring speech\" at the beginning.
    • \n
  • Change the active verb form \"wrote\" to \"was written\" (past simple passive).
    • \n
  • Add the preposition \"by\" followed by the original subject \"him.\"
    • \n
  • Ensure the phrase \"for the event\" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
    • \n
\n\n
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
\n\n
 
\n\n
Correct Sentence: \"An inspiring speech was written by him for the event.\"
\n\n
 
\n\n
Additional Information
\n\n
    \n
  • Option 1: \"An inspiring speech was being written by him for the event.\" – Incorrect tense (past continuous passive).
    • \n
  • Option 3: \"An inspiring speech is written by him for the event.\" – Incorrect tense (present simple passive).
    • \n
  • Option 4: \"An inspiring speech has been written by him for the event.\" – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).
    • \n

        Key Points
        \n\n

        • The context indicates that Federico's academic experience of isolation was partly due to his own personal tendency.
          • \n\t

        \n\n
         
        \n\n
        Complete Passage: The mathematician Federico Ardila-Mantilla grew up in Colombia, an indifferent student but gifted in math. He was failing most of his classes at his high school in Bogotá when someone suggested him to apply to MIT. He had not heard of the school. To his surprise, he got in, and he went on scholarship. Mathematically, he did well. One of his professors, an acid-tongued theoretician known to compare his audience to a herd of cows, routinely tucked 'open' math problems into homework assignments, without telling the students. These had never been solved by anyone. Ardila solved one. He went on to receive his bachelor's and Ph.D. in math from MIT. But his academic experience was also one of isolation. Part of it had to do with his own introversion. Part of it was cultural. As a Latino, he was very much in the minority in the department, and he did not feel comfortable in American mathematical spaces. No one had tried to explicitly exclude him, yet he felt alone. In math, collaborating with others opens up new kinds of learning and thinking. But in his nine years at MIT, Ardila worked with others only twice.
        \n\n
         
        \n\n
        Additional Information
        \n\n
          \n\t
        • Molestation (छेड़खानी): 'Molestation' means the action of pestering or harassing someone, typically in an aggressive or persistent manner, which does not fit the context.
          • \n\t
        • Quantification (मात्रांकन): 'Quantification' means the expression or measurement of the quantity of something, which is unrelated to expressing a personal tendency.
          • \n\t
        • Interrogation (पूछताछ): 'Interrogation' means the action of interrogating or questioning someone, which does not fit the context of describing a personal tendency.
          • \n

        Complete Passage: The mathematician Federico Ardila-Mantilla grew up in Colombia, an indifferent student but gifted in math. He was failing most of his classes at his high school in Bogotá when someone suggested him to apply to MIT. He had not heard of the school. To his surprise, he got in, and he went on scholarship. Mathematically, he did well. One of his professors, an acid-tongued theoretician known to compare his audience to a herd of cows, routinely tucked 'open' math problems into homework assignments, without telling the students. These had never been solved by anyone. Ardila solved one. He went on to receive his bachelor's and Ph.D. in math from MIT. But his academic experience was also one of isolation. Part of it had to do with his own introversion. Part of it was cultural. As a Latino, he was very much in the minority in the department, and he did not feel comfortable in American mathematical spaces. No one had tried to explicitly exclude him, yet he felt alone. In math, collaborating with others opens up new kinds of learning and thinking. But in his nine years at MIT, Ardila worked with others only twice.
